description: Dead bug guide: lower opposite arm and leg with your back flat to train the deep abs. Covers how it should feel, mistakes, easier and harder versions.
intro: The dead bug is a slow core exercise done on your back: you lower one arm and the opposite leg while your trunk stays still. It does not train the pelvic floor directly, but it teaches your deep abdominals to work with your breath, which supports the pelvis from above.
feel: You should feel a steady, low effort deep in your belly. You should not feel your lower back arch, your neck strain or your breath stop. Slide a hand under your lower back: if the gap grows as the leg lowers, the range is too big. Keep the pelvic floor relaxed, not clenched.

mistakes.wrong: Holding your breath during each reach
mistakes.right: Breathe out as the arm and leg lower and breathe in as they return.

mistakes.wrong: Moving fast and swinging the limbs
mistakes.right: Take about three seconds to lower and three to return, so the abs do the work instead of momentum.

mistakes.wrong: Pushing the belly out or bearing down
mistakes.right: Draw the lower belly gently in and up, never down into the pelvis. If you feel pressure low down, reduce the range.

easier: Keep your arms on the floor and lower one leg at a time, tapping the heel down with the knee bent.
harder: Straighten the leg fully as it lowers, or add a gentle Kegel on each exhale and fully relax on the inhale.
who: Useful for desk workers, lifters who want a stable trunk, and anyone returning to exercise who needs a low-load start.
skip: Check with a doctor or pelvic floor physiotherapist first after recent abdominal or pelvic surgery, if you notice doming along the middle of your belly, or if you are pregnant or recently gave birth. If back pain sharpens, reduce the range. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Is the dead bug good for the pelvic floor?
faq.a: Indirectly. It trains the deep abdominals and breathing that work alongside the pelvic floor, so pair it with separate Kegels.

faq.q: Why does my lower back lift off the floor?
faq.a: Your abs cannot yet control that range. Lower the leg less far, bend the knee more and move slower until the back stays down.
